findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Promote 'bounded-live validation' to an acceptance criterion: exercise the defaulted scoped-runtime Jira write and Git push/delivery path end-to-end against a real (bounded-live) boundary before cutover, not only verified-fake substitutes.
evidence: 'End-to-end verified-fake Cloud/DC runs cover create/update/comment/link/delete/inbound apply plus Git commit/push/delivery'
AC1: 'Verified-fake Cloud/DC apply plus Git/delivery paths complete with ambient resolvers poisoned'
'Until bounded-live validation, a compatibility facade may invoke the legacy write path' — bounded-live is referenced but not an acceptance criterion
E5 cutover/proxy-validation: an acceptance criterion satisfiable by offline-only coverage that never exercises the defaulted path live lets the work close green while the live path is broken
findings.finding: This is a cutover that makes the scoped-runtime write/apply, Git push, and ACLI/delivery paths the new default, but every acceptance criterion is satisfiable by 'verified-fake' Cloud/DC runs that substitute for the live Jira/Git boundary. 'Bounded-live validation' is named only in the Compatibility/rollback section as a pre-cutover gate, not tied to any acceptance criterion, so the suite can close green while the defaulted live path is never exercised end-to-end against a real Jira/Git remote.
findings.location: Testing (RED -> GREEN) first bullet; Acceptance Criteria line 1; Compatibility/rollback 'bounded-live validation'
scenarios: Scoped-runtime write path defaults on; verified-fake tests pass; a real Jira Cloud write or Git push under the threaded runtime fails (e.g. overlay env not actually applied to the child, or push targets wrong remote) but no acceptance gate catches it because bounded-live validation is not a closing criterion.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC requiring a bounded-live Cloud/DC apply + Git push + delivery run under the S2 runtime (with ambient resolvers poisoned) as a precondition for flipping the write facade to the scoped path.

secret_screen.py:32-33 docstring already warns a second table risks drift: 'rather than keeping a second, drifting table.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify the _child_env.py selective-removal policy against the established least-privilege/allowlist remedy for subprocess secret leakage (cite prior art), and address the fail-open risk when the exact-name registry is incomplete/stale (e.g. document why an allowlist floor was rejected or add a registry-completeness guard).
evidence: Outcome: 'unrelated siblings remove exact secret names declared by other Rebar adapters, unknown native Git/SSH/AWS/proxy/CA variables survive'

Web (retrieved): CVE-2026-45370 / GHSA-5v57-8rxj-3p2r describe full-process-environment exposure to CLI subprocesses because _prepare_environment() copied the entire host env — the documented remedy is minimal/allowlisted env, not copy-then-remove-known-names

Codebase: existing child-env builds copy the full env today (git_fetch.py:263 `{**os.environ, ...}`, repo_snapshot.py:354/381, push.py:190/246, acli_subprocess.py:311 `return os.environ.copy()`, enrich_drain.py:256) — the plan consolidates but keeps a copy-then-scrub default rather than an allowlist floor
ABSENCE: the plan states no rationale for choosing selective-removal over an allowlist and does not address the fail-open risk of an incomplete/stale exact-name registry
findings.finding: The new _child_env.py adopts a security-critical env-projection POLICY (ambient inheritance + removal of only EXACT declared secret names for unrelated siblings, with unknown native variables preserved) without considering the established least-privilege/allowlist approach that prior art recommends for exactly this subprocess-secret-leakage class; a denylist keyed on a checked-in exact-name registry fails open when a Rebar-owned secret name is missing, renamed, or newly added.
findings.location: Plan step 2 ('a checked-in registry of exact secret names owned by each Rebar adapter') and Outcome paragraph ('unrelated siblings remove exact secret names declared by other Rebar adapters, unknown native ... variables survive')
scenarios: A future Rebar adapter secret env var is added but not registered, so it leaks into an unrelated sibling child's environment
An operator-set secret-bearing variable that is not a 'declared' Rebar name (e.g. a custom token consumed by a native SDK chain) is inherited by every sibling because unknown variables 'survive'
